marks.gloss_en: ומה לעשות שלום בין איש לאשתו אמרה תורה: שמי שנכתב בקדושה ימחה על המים; לעשות שלום לכל העולם כולו -- על אחת כמה וכמה
David: whoever knows what to say and does not say it, let him be strangled in his throat
שמע מינה -- from 'he set it at a thousand cubits', the earth above the deep is a thousand cubits thick
והא חזינן דכרינן פורתא ונפקי מיא -- but we see that we dig a little and water comes out
ההוא מסולמא דפרת -- that [water] is from the ascent of the Euphrates
he wrote the Name on a shard and cast it into the deep, and the deep went down sixteen thousand cubits
the verse clause: 'their backs toward the Sanctuary of the Lord, and their faces eastward' (Ezek 8:16) -- whose first half is probed as redundant
it teaches that they would uncover themselves and excrete downward
איני?! והאמר רבי זירא: כל האומר שמע שמע כאילו אמר מודים מודים -- how could they say 'to Yah' twice in a row? (kind svara: no objection kind exists for an amoraic-memra contradiction)
אלא הכי אמרי: המה משתחוים קדמה, ואנו ליה (אנחנו מודים), ועינינו ליה מיחלות -- the two mentions are not adjacent (= p_nusach_hema_mishtachavim)
R' Zeira: whoever says 'Shema, Shema' is as if he said 'Modim, Modim'
the mishna lemma: and priests stood at the upper gate that descends [from the Israelites' Courtyard to the Women's Courtyard], etc.
one does not sound fewer than twenty-one blasts in the Temple
and on Shabbat eve they would add six: three to stop the people from work, and three to distinguish between holy and profane

on a Shabbat eve within the Festival there were forty-eight: three for the opening of the gates, three for the upper gate, three for the lower gate, three for the filling of the water, three on the altar, nine for the morning tamid, nine for the afternoon tamid, nine for the additional offerings, three to stop the people from work, and three to distinguish between holy and profane
דתניא: R' Yehuda's seven-to-sixteen against the mishnah's twenty-one-to-forty-eight
the mishnah is not in accordance with R' Yehuda
ורבי יהודה, לפניה ולאחריה מנליה? -- the Rabbanan read his verse as the source of the plain blasts around the terua; if he spends it on 'one blast', from where does he get them?
נפקא ליה מ״שנית״ (= p_yehuda_shenit)
R' Yehuda's reason: the verse says 'and you shall sound (utkatem) a terua', and it is written 'a terua they shall sound (yitke'u)' -- how so? tekia and terua are one
ורבנן מאי טעמייהו? ובהקהיל את הקהל תתקעו ולא תריעו -- ואי סלקא דעתך תקיעה תרועה אחת היא, אמר רחמנא פלגא דמצוה עביד ופלגא לא עביד?! (the stam giving the Rabbanan's reason)

ורבי יהודה: ההוא לסימנא בעלמא הוא דאתא (= p_behakhil_lesimana). The Rabbanan's rejoinder at 53b.13 -- סימנא הוא ורחמנא שוייה מצוה (p_simana_veshavyeh_mitzva) -- attacks this answer; the schema cannot attack an answer (header)
the Rabbanan's reason: it is written 'and when assembling the congregation you shall sound a tekia and not a terua'
the Rabbanan: it is a signal, and the Merciful One made it a mitzva
